description:
Golden test vectors for canonical JSON digest (json-digest spec).
  Each vector tests: SHA3-256 hashing with multibase Base64Url encoding
  and 'cj' prefix, following the iop-rs Rust reference implementation.
  The digest function recursively masks sub-objects with their content
  hashes before hashing the top-level flattened form.

  Rust reference (iop-rs): test_json_digest, reject_non_nfkd tests in
  json-digest/src/digest.rs.

  Verified against Rust reference implementation for vectors labeled
  cjo-verified: true.

vectors.description: Flat object with primitive values. No recursive masking.
Empty object, no properties to mask.

Object with nested sub-object and array values.
      Sub-objects and arrays are recursively masked before
      the top-level hash is computed.

Rust TestData { b: 1, a: 2 } -> canonical keys sorted.
      Verified against iop-rs test_json_digest.

NFKD-normalized key. Rust reject_non_nfkd test:
      key 'a\\u0301lom' (a + combining acute).
      Input keys MUST be NFKD-normalized per iop-rs convention.

A JSON string value digests to itself. The Rust test
      passes &str "\"cjuzC-...\"" (with embedded double quotes) to
      digest_data; serde serializes it as a JSON string value, and
      selective_digest_json returns it unchanged. Idempotent for any
      string regardless of content.

IEEE 754 canonicalization: 0.1 in decimal notation
      remains 0.1. Verifies that the shortest round-trip
      representation is used for simple floats.

IEEE 754 canonicalization: 4.2E-5 (scientific notation)
      canonicalizes to 0.000042 in decimal. Verifies that
      exponent notation is expanded to the shortest decimal form.

Rust-vs-TS canonicalization difference: 3.0 has a
      trailing decimal-zero in the input. TS round-trips
      through f64 and emits 3 (the shortest representation),
      while Rust preserves the original 3.0 text via
      serde_json Number. This vector captures the TS side
      as reference when fixing the Rust implementation.

Rust-vs-TS canonicalization difference: 65.50 has
      trailing zero in the decimal part. TS canonicalizes
      to 65.5 (shortest round-trip), while Rust preserves
      the original 65.50 text. Reference vector for the
      Rust-side fix.

Rust-vs-TS canonicalization: 3.0E+30 (large positive
      exponent). JS emits 3e+30 (with + sign). Ryu-based
      serializers emit 3e30 (without +). This vector targets
      the JS convention; Rust side must add the + to match.

Rust-vs-TS canonicalization: 5.40E-21 (tiny negative
      exponent). Both JS and Ryu emit 5.4e-21 (with - sign).
      Already aligned — reference to confirm agreement.

Large number boundary (n=21): 1e20 is the largest
      exact power of 10 still rendered in decimal notation
      by ECMAScript (21 digits). Ryu may emit scientific
      "1e+20" since it is shorter. Reference: TS output.

Large number boundary (n=22): 1e21 is the smallest
      exact power of 10 rendered in scientific notation by
      ECMAScript. Ryu also uses scientific but omits +.
      Reference: TS convention includes +.

Small number boundary (n=-5): 1e-6 is the smallest
      positive value rendered in 0.000... decimal notation
      by ECMAScript. Ryu may emit scientific "1e-6" since
      it is shorter. Reference: TS output.

Small number boundary (n=-6): 1e-7 is the smallest
      positive value rendered in scientific notation by
      ECMAScript. Ryu also emits 1e-7. Both agree.

Integer-valued float with trailing zeros: 100.00
      carries no fractional part. TS canonicalizes to 100
      (integer). Rust preserves 100.00 via serde_json
      Number::Float. Reference for Rust-side fix.

IEEE 754 double precision boundary: 1.2345678901234567
      has 17 significant digits (the maximum for reliable
      round-trip). Both JS and Ryu produce the same output.
      Trailing zeros after the 17th digit are lost.

Trailing zeros in the decimal part: 0.001000 has two
      trailing zeros after the significant digits. TS
      strips them to 0.001 (shortest representation).
      Rust preserves the original text. Reference for
      Rust-side fix.

selectiveVectors.description: Keep the y subtree open and mask z. Verified against iop-rs test_selective_digesting.
Keep nested y.z open and mask siblings. Verified against iop-rs test_selective_digesting.

Selective disclosure with float values: keep .a subtree
      open and mask .b. Verifies float canonicalization in
      selective disclosure context.
